## Declarations and implementations

```plato
//==
// # Polygons
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Polygons — planar polygon, hole, set, and star bodies
//  - Planar-polygon kernels in space
//  - Polyline length and deformation
//  - Planar-polygon-in-space, prism, and pyramid bodies

library Polygons
{
    //==
    // # Polygons — planar polygon, hole, set, and star bodies
    //
    // Area, perimeter, bounds, centroid, containment, nearest-point and support bodies
    // for the types declared in `polygons.types.plato` (`LIBRARIES.md` ground rules 1 and 10).
    // The 2D ring kernels — shoelace area, area centroid, even-odd containment, chain
    // length, chain projection — live in `geometry.library.plato` and are not
    // respelled here.
    //
    // Conventions fixed here:
    //
    //   * WINDING: counter-clockwise boundaries enclose positive area; holes wind
    //     opposite to the boundary that contains them. The hole-aware bodies below rely
    //     only on the DECLARED containment invariants, never on the stored hole winding —
    //     `Area(PolygonWithHoles2D)` subtracts absolute hole areas rather than adding
    //     signed ones, so a hole stored with the wrong winding still subtracts.
    //   * `Area` is NON-NEGATIVE everywhere. `SignedArea(Polygon2D)` is offered
    //     separately for callers that need the orientation; it is the raw shoelace value,
    //     which for a self-intersecting ring is the winding-weighted area, not the area
    //     of the covered point set.
    //   * CONTAINMENT is the even-odd rule, so a point exactly on a boundary edge is not
    //     classified reliably.
    //   * `Perimeter` of a region with holes counts EVERY boundary component: the outer
    //     ring plus every hole ring. Likewise `Perimeter(PolygonSet2D)` sums all
    //     components.

    //==
    // # Polygon2D and ConvexPolygon2D

    // The SIGNED shoelace area: positive for counter-clockwise winding, negative
    // for clockwise. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoelace_formula
    SignedArea(p: Polygon2D): Number
        => p.Points.ShoelaceArea;

    // The enclosed area, always non-negative.
    Area(p: Polygon2D): Number
        => p.Points.ShoelaceArea.Abs;

    // The total boundary length, including the closing edge.
    Perimeter(p: Polygon2D): Number
        => p.Points.ChainLength(true);

    // The area centroid (NOT the mean of the vertices).
    Centroid(p: Polygon2D): Point2D
        => p.Points.PolygonAreaCentroid;

    // Even-odd containment.
    Contains(p: Polygon2D, point: Point2D): Boolean
        => p.Points.PolygonContainsPoint(point);

    // The query point when it lies in the polygon, otherwise the nearest point of
    // the boundary.
    ClosestPoint(p: Polygon2D, point: Point2D): Point2D
        => p.Contains(point) ? point : p.Points.ClosestPointOnChain(true, point);

    // The polygon with every vertex carried through the mapping.
    Deform(p: Polygon2D, mapping: Function1<Point2D, Point2D>): Polygon2D
        => Polygon2D(p.Points.Map(mapping));

    // The enclosed area. Non-negative; the convex invariant does not change the
    // formula, only guarantees the ring is simple.
    Area(p: ConvexPolygon2D): Number
        => p.Points.ShoelaceArea.Abs;

    // The total boundary length.
    Perimeter(p: ConvexPolygon2D): Number
        => p.Points.ChainLength(true);

    // The area centroid.
    Centroid(p: ConvexPolygon2D): Point2D
        => p.Points.PolygonAreaCentroid;

    // Even-odd containment. A half-plane sweep would exploit convexity, but the
    // even-odd test is already exact for a simple ring and needs no winding
    // assumption.
    Contains(p: ConvexPolygon2D, point: Point2D): Boolean
        => p.Points.PolygonContainsPoint(point);

    // The query point when it lies in the polygon, otherwise the nearest boundary
    // point.
    ClosestPoint(p: ConvexPolygon2D, point: Point2D): Point2D
        => p.Contains(point) ? point : p.Points.ClosestPointOnChain(true, point);

    // The vertex farthest along `direction`. Exact because the polygon is convex,
    // so a support point is always a vertex. Linear scan, not the binary search the
    // declaration's "constant-cost support mapping" note anticipates.
    // TODO(content): binary search over the convex vertex ring.
    Support(p: ConvexPolygon2D, direction: Direction2D): Point2D
        => p.Points.Reduce(p.Points.First, (best, v) =>
            direction.Vector.Dot(v.PositionVector) > direction.Vector.Dot(best.PositionVector)
                ? v : best);

    // The polygon with every vertex carried through the mapping. Convexity is NOT
    // re-checked; a non-affine mapping can break the type's invariant.
    Deform(p: ConvexPolygon2D, mapping: Function1<Point2D, Point2D>): ConvexPolygon2D
        => ConvexPolygon2D(p.Points.Map(mapping));

    //==
    // # PolygonWithHoles2D

    // The boundary's area less every hole's area.
    Area(r: PolygonWithHoles2D): Number
        => r.Boundary.Area - SumOf(r.Holes.Map(h => h.Area));

    // EVERY boundary component: the outer ring plus every hole ring.
    Perimeter(r: PolygonWithHoles2D): Number
        => r.Boundary.Perimeter + SumOf(r.Holes.Map(h => h.Perimeter));

    // The area-weighted centroid of the boundary minus the holes: each hole
    // contributes its centroid with a NEGATIVE weight.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centroid#By_geometric_decomposition
    // Precondition: the net area is non-zero.
    Centroid(r: PolygonWithHoles2D): Point2D
    {
        var boundaryArea = r.Boundary.Area;
        var holeAreas = r.Holes.Map(h => h.Area);
        var net = boundaryArea - SumOf(holeAreas);
        var centre = r.Boundary.Centroid;
        var cx = centre.X * boundaryArea
            - SumOf(r.Holes.Count.MapRange(i => r.Holes[i].Centroid.X * holeAreas[i]));
        var cy = centre.Y * boundaryArea
            - SumOf(r.Holes.Count.MapRange(i => r.Holes[i].Centroid.Y * holeAreas[i]));
        return (cx / net, cy / net);
    }

    // The bounds of the outer boundary; the holes lie strictly inside it.
    Bounds(r: PolygonWithHoles2D): Bounds2D
        => r.Boundary.Bounds;

    // Inside the boundary and outside every hole.
    Contains(r: PolygonWithHoles2D, point: Point2D): Boolean
        => r.Boundary.Contains(point) && r.Holes.Any(h => h.Contains(point)).Not;

    // The region with the boundary and every hole carried through the mapping.
    Deform(r: PolygonWithHoles2D, mapping: Function1<Point2D, Point2D>): PolygonWithHoles2D
        => (r.Boundary.Deform(mapping), r.Holes.Map(h => h.Deform(mapping)));

    //==
    // # PolygonSet2D
    //
    // The components are mutually disjoint, so every measure is a plain sum and
    // containment is a disjunction.

    // The summed area of the components.
    Area(s: PolygonSet2D): Number
        => SumOf(s.Polygons.Map(p => p.Area));
```
